quotes.text: While it's great to see Nvidia finally establish a compliance function to oversee national security and export controls, the lack of a plot prior compliance function is supportive of our fear that federal and congressional investigations may reveal that backdoor sales to China represented a meaningf

For what it's worth, we believe that it will, it just may not arrive in time to prevent a lower low in the current risk-off market regime.

quotes.text: A concern of mine is that we are going to get a bunch of standard Fedspeak and that these task forces are just going to tell the Fed what they already know.
The Fed is somewhat unique. There are other central banks like the Bank of England last year that had a 441 vote, and that was considered okay.
I think it's more of a feature because part of the uncertainty that we're getting is not just because we're not getting specific Fedspeak, it's because we're getting uncertain data.
We're getting the Fed saying that they're committed to their two percent target and we can't get inflation under three.
The stock market, the S&P was up 2 and a half percent, and 10 year yields were up 30 basis points in the same week.
I've been one that's argued that 5% yield is fine, that the economy's fine with it, I even would argue the housing market's fine with it, and the stock market's fine with it.
If the data was more consistent and more dovish for the Fed, you know, quieter inflation that would suggest that they don't need to move, I think that that premium would go away.

key_points.point: The Fed faces a new era of uncertainty with divided opinions among policymakers and conflicting economic data.
Task forces created by the Fed will likely just reiterate what officials already know.
Other central banks like the Bank of England have had split votes without disrupting market expectations.
Current market uncertainty stems from conflicting data as well as lack of clear Fedspeak.
If economic data were more consistently dovish and showed quieter inflation, term premium would likely disappear.
key_points.condition: if data was more consistent and dovish

key_points.point: The economy, housing market, and stock market can function well with 5 percent yields.
Demand for compute and AI buildout will cause computing and chip demand to skyrocket over the next couple of years.
A successful IPO will come to market without creating major market hiccups.
